npcs.name: Mira
npcs.title: Merchant
lines: Potions, food, scrolls — and I buy whatever the monsters leave behind!

npcs.name: Bren
npcs.title: Craftsman
lines: Good cloth, good steel. That's all a man needs.

npcs.name: Master Gareth
npcs.title: Warrior Master
lines: A blade is only as strong as the will that holds it.
Grow stronger, young one. When you are ready, the path of the Warrior will be waiting.

npcs.name: Master Seraphine
npcs.title: Book Mage Master
lines: Every page of this book holds a storm. Few can read it.
Come back when your mind is ready, and I will teach you the path of the Book Mage.

npcs.name: Master Lyra
npcs.title: Archer Master
lines: Patience. The arrow flies true only for those who wait.
When you are ready, the path of the Archer will be open to you.

npcs.name: Master Hayato
npcs.title: Samurai Master
lines: One cut. One breath. Nothing more.
Return when your spirit is calm, and I will show you the path of the Samurai.

npcs.name: Guard Cassian
npcs.title: Temple Guard
lines: Halt. Beyond this gate stand the Masters of the four paths.
Only those strong enough to cross the Crimson Ruins may seek them.

npcs.name: Guard Darius
npcs.title: Temple Guard
lines: The cursed swordsmen never pass this gate. Not while I stand here.
Go on. The Masters are waiting by the great stairs.

npcs.name: Nimbus
npcs.title: Keeper of Cloud Haven
lines: Ho ho! A visitor, all the way up here? Welcome to Cloud Haven, little traveller.
Mind the Pufflings — they mean no harm. They just love to nibble my cloud.

npcs.name: Solenne
npcs.title: Keeper of the Sun
lines: Welcome to the Sun Shrine, traveller. You carry the sun's warmth — I can feel it.
The pedestal behind me is empty. Something precious once shone there...

npcs.name: Lumen
npcs.title: The Lamplighter
lines: Evening, traveller. I light the lanterns along this walk, every dusk, same as my father did.
Mind the Glowcaps. Sweet little things, but they bump my lanterns out.

npcs.name: Bram
npcs.title: Root Warden
lines: The Elder Tree's door. Sealed since the Heart was stolen; it answers only to the sun's warmth.

npcs.name: Wren
npcs.title: Archer Mentor
lines: Welcome to Elderwood Village, traveller. Every archer on this side of the mountains learned to draw a bow on that range.
Mind the Glowcaps on the walk. They bounce, but they're harmless if you keep your distance.

npcs.name: Hazel
npcs.title: Village Merchant
lines: Potions, snacks, a scroll or two! Hazel's got what a hero needs.
Everything on this tray was bottled right here under the Elder Tree.

quests.title: First Steps
offer: Welcome, young one. I am Aldric — I train those who arrive at the Legacy Courtyard.
Every hero starts small. Just east of here, the Ivy Terraces have been overrun by Ivy Sproutlings.
Clear ten of them, then come back and tell me what you learned.
progress: The Ivy Terraces are just east of the Courtyard. Ten Ivy Sproutlings — I'll be here.
done: Ten of them! Your sword arm is waking up.
Now for something with a blade of its own.
quests.summary: Master Aldric asked you to clear the Ivy Sproutlings from the Ivy Terraces.

quests.title: The Sealed Road
quests.summary: Master Aldric told you why the road east is shut: the Masters sealed the Sun Gate against the Curse, and it opens only for one who has crossed the sun. He sent you up to Nimbus, the old cloud above the terraces.
offer: Well done. Now listen. Long ago the Curse rose in the east, and it turned the Courtyard's own guard to rust.

The Masters shut the golden Sun Gate to keep it from us. Its lock opens only for one who has crossed the low sun of Sunfall Pass: the sun's warmth stays with them, and the Curse cannot take hold of a warm heart.

No path on the ground leads there. Climb the stone steps up the Ivy Heights, walk on to the summit and step out onto the clouds. At the end of them lives Nimbus, a kind old cloud. Tell him Aldric sent you.
progress: Up the stone steps of the Ivy Heights, over the summit, along the clouds to Nimbus.
done: Aldric sent you? Ho ho, then you're very welcome up here, little traveller!

objectives.text: Find Nimbus (Cloud Haven, over the Sky Path)

quests.title: The Training Grounds
offer: You crossed the sun! I felt the Sun Gate open from here. Carry that warmth with you: east of it the Curse is still strong.
Just past the gate lie the old Training Grounds. Our guard drilled there until the Curse turned them to rust, and the Rusted Swordsmen drill there still. Set fifteen of them free.
Then walk on to Sunstone Plaza and find Mira. She'll want to meet you.
progress: Fifteen Rusted Swordsmen in the Training Grounds, then Mira in Sunstone Plaza.
done: Aldric sent you? Then you're worth knowing!
quests.summary: Master Aldric sent you to the Rusted Swordsmen of the Training Grounds, and on to Mira in Sunstone Plaza.

quests.title: Rust for Coin
offer: Now — I sell a little of everything to whoever passes through the plaza.
Those Rusted Swordsmen in the Training Grounds drop shards of their old blades. Smiths pay me good coin for them.
Bring me ten Rust Shards and I'll make it worth your while — and open my shelves to you.
progress: Ten Rust Shards from the Rusted Swordsmen, east in the Training Grounds. Walk over them to pick them up!
done: Ten shards — perfect! Here, take these for the road.
From now on you can trade with me any time. Anything a monster drops, I'll buy.
quests.summary: Mira the merchant wants ten Rust Shards from the Rusted Swordsmen.

quests.title: Thorns in the Orchard
offer: The Old Orchard past the plaza used to give me the sweetest oranges in the land.
Now Thornlings crawl all over it. Clear fifteen of them and the trees can breathe again.
progress: The Old Orchard is east of the plaza. Fifteen Thornlings!
done: The orchard's quiet again — thank you! Take these, fresh from the trees.
And a Swift Potion for the road: the Crimson Ruins are further than they look.
quests.summary: Mira wants the Thornlings cleared from the Old Orchard.

quests.title: Cloth of the Cursed
offer: Hm. You're the one who's been clearing out the training grounds, eh? Name's Bren. I mend banners for the Temple.
The Cursed Swordsmen in the Crimson Ruins wear cloth that still hums with their curse. I can wash it clean and weave it again.
Fifteen scraps of Cursed Cloth. Do that, and I'll fill your belly and sharpen your arm.
progress: Fifteen scraps of Cursed Cloth from the Cursed Swordsmen in the Crimson Ruins, past the Old Orchard.
done: Fifteen! The curse is weaker than I feared. Here — my wife's cakes, and a Warrior Potion.
Drink the potion before a hard fight. Your blade will bite deeper for a while.
quests.summary: Bren the craftsman needs fifteen scraps of Cursed Cloth from the Cursed Swordsmen.

quests.title: The Gate Warden
offer: The Temple's old gate has a keeper now — a Warden twisted by the Curse. Nobody passes him.
Bring him down and the road to the Masters is open. Bring me back his word that it's done.
progress: The Gate Warden waits at the Ruined Gate, past the Crimson Ruins. Mind his reach.
done: The Warden — fallen? Then the gate is ours again. Here, you've earned this.
quests.summary: Bren asked you to bring down the Gate Warden at the Ruined Gate.

quests.title: Before the Road
offer: You've grown, but the Temple Road is no place for a beginner.
Reach level 10, then come back to me. I'll see you're ready for the Masters.
progress: Level 10 — then come back. The Rusted and the Cursed Swordsmen will teach you well.
done: Level 10. Good. The four Masters wait at the far end of the Temple Road — one of them will take you as a student.
Past the Masters, east of the Temple Road, lies Elderwood Village in the twilight gardens. Wren keeps the archers' range there; she'll have work for anyone with a steady hand.
Take these. Blue Potions for your skills, and a Return Scroll: read it and it carries you back here.
quests.summary: Master Aldric wants you to reach level 10 before you walk the Temple Road.

quests.title: Lost Puffs
quests.summary: Nimbus asked you to bring back 15 Cloud Puffs the Pufflings nibbled off Cloud Haven.
offer: Ho ho... you see these holes in my cloud? The Pufflings nibble it, bit by bit — little rascals.
Could you bring me back fifteen Cloud Puffs? Just tap the Pufflings gently, they drop them.
Do that, and I'll give you a feather of my own — it'll carry you up here whenever you like.
progress: Fifteen Cloud Puffs, little traveller. The Pufflings bounce about all over Cloud Haven.
done: Oh, wonderful! Look how soft they are — my cloud will be good as new.
Here, take these feathers. Hold one up to the sky and the wind will bring you home to me.

objectives.text: Collect Cloud Puffs from Pufflings (Cloud Haven)

quests.title: Cheer Up, Big Grumble
quests.summary: Nimbus asked you to cheer up Big Grumble, the sulky cloud east of Cloud Haven. His gift lets you pass the sun.
offer: Hmm... can you hear that huffing? That's Big Grumble, at the east end of Cloud Haven.
He's not bad — just a very grumpy cloud. When he's in a mood he blows everyone off their feet.
Give him a good bout and he'll puff out his bad mood. He always feels better after!
progress: Big Grumble wanders by the great cloud wall on the right. He comes back every couple of minutes.
done: Ho ho! He's smiling again — I can see it from here.
And look what he left you: a Cloud Form. Uncork it and you'll be light as a cloud...
...light enough to slip past the low sun of Sunfall Pass, just east of here. Few have seen what lies beyond!
The sun's light will stay with you once you've crossed it. That's what the old gate below is waiting for.

quests.title: The Stolen Sun
quests.summary: Solenne, Keeper of the Sun, told you the Heart of the Sun was stolen from her shrine. The Sunbeams keep what is left of its light: bring her three Sun Shards.
offer: Long ago the Heart of the Sun shone on this pedestal, and its light kept the whole land warm.
One dark night it was stolen. As its light faded, the Curse crept in from the east: that is how it all began.
A little of its light still lingers in the Sunbeams floating round the shrine. Tap them gently and they let go of a Sun Shard. Bring me three, and I'll make you something to carry its warmth.
progress: Three Sun Shards. The Sunbeams float all round the shrine.
done: Three Sun Shards... feel how warm they are. Here: I set them in an amulet for you.
Whoever took the Heart went east. Past the Sun Gate stands the Temple Gate, where the Masters keep watch. Tell them the Keeper of the Sun sent you.

objectives.text: Collect Sun Shards from Sunbeams (Afterglow Rest)

quests.title: Steady Hands
quests.summary: Wren, the archer mentor of Elderwood Village, asked you to thin the Glowcaps along Wisteria Walk so the young archers can practise in peace.
offer: New in the village? Then let me put you to work. My students can't practise with Glowcaps bouncing off the targets.
Clear eight of them off Wisteria Walk, west of the gate, and come back. Lumen the lamplighter will thank you too.
progress: Eight Glowcaps on Wisteria Walk, just west of the village gate.
done: Eight already? Steady hands. Here, a few things from Hazel's tray, on me.

quests.title: Lights Out
quests.summary: Lumen the Lamplighter asked you to thin out the Glowcaps that keep bumping his lanterns out along Wisteria Walk.
offer: Evening, traveller. The twilight gardens are lovely, aren't they? I light every lantern on this walk, dusk after dusk.
Trouble is, the Glowcaps have been bouncing about and bumping my lanterns out faster than I can light them.
Would you thin them out a little? Twelve of them should calm the walk. They only hop and puff, nothing worse.
progress: Twelve Glowcaps, along Wisteria Walk. Gently does it.
done: Ah, the lanterns stay lit! Thank you. Here, Bren's wife sent me more cake than one lamplighter can eat.
Now... while you were out there, did you see a fox? A grey one, with a little light at its neck?

quests.title: Moth Dust
quests.summary: Lumen saw a grey fox run east with a warm light at its neck. He needs ten Moth Dust from the Lantern Moths to make a lantern that can show the way to the Hollow Gate.
offer: The night the Sun Shrine's light went out, a grey fox ran past me, east, with a warm little light swinging at its neck.
It went for the Hollow Gate, past the Lantern Steps. The gate is sealed, but the fox keeps slipping about there, hard to see in the dusk.
Bring me ten Moth Dust from the Lantern Moths and I'll make you a Dusk Lantern. Its light shows what hides in the twilight.
progress: Ten Moth Dust, from the Lantern Moths on the Lantern Steps. They shed it when they're startled.
done: Perfect, see how it shimmers. A moment... there. A Dusk Lantern, lit with moth light.
Carry it to the Hollow Gate. Whatever hides there will show itself in its light.

objectives.text: Collect Moth Dust from Lantern Moths (Lantern Steps)

quests.title: The Shade Fox
quests.summary: With the Dusk Lantern lit, Lumen sent you to the Hollow Gate to catch the Shade Fox and take back the warm light it carries.
offer: The fox is at the Hollow Gate, I'm sure of it. With the Dusk Lantern you'll see it plain.
It's quick and it's clever, but it's only a fox. Tire it out, and whatever it carries at its neck, bring it to me.
progress: The Hollow Gate, at the end of the Lantern Steps. The Shade Fox is quick, so mind its tail.
done: You caught it! And look... a Sun Ember. A piece of the Heart of the Sun itself, still warm.
The fox was a thief's pet, not the thief. Whoever holds the rest of the Heart is beyond the Hollow Gate... and that door needs more than a lantern.
Keep the Ember close. When the way opens, you'll want its warmth.

objectives.text: Defeat the Shade Fox (The Elder Hollow)

quests.title: Into the Den
quests.summary: Wren told you the Sun Ember can open the Elder Tree's sealed door: the thieves' den lies inside. Clear it with Bram's leave and bring back what the magpie stole.
offer: That Ember of yours... I've seen the Elder Tree's door glow like that. The fox was only a pet; its master nests INSIDE the tree.
Bram the Root Warden keeps the door. Show him the Ember. Five chambers, he says, and a thieving magpie at the end. Take friends if you can find them: the den is meant for a party.
Come back when you've been through, and tell me what you found.
progress: Bram stands before the Elder Tree's door, east of here. Show him the Ember.
done: Two Embers! Then the Heart truly is in pieces, scattered by thieves. You've done what no archer of this village has.
Rest, then. When the next piece shows itself, you'll be the first I tell.

objectives.text: Clear the Thief's Den (the Elder Tree's door, with Bram)

idle: You've done well. The Masters wait at the end of the Temple Road.
